author: Palmetto State News
title: South Carolina men's track and field earns two All-American honors at NCAA Outdoor Championship
text:
South Carolina Men’s Track & Field concluded its outdoor season on June 10 during the semifinal day of the NCAA Outdoor Championship at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon.
Devan Crumpton and Jaouad Khchina represented the Gamecocks in their respective events, each earning Second Team All-American honors. Crumpton finished 16th overall in the 400 meters with a time of 45.76 seconds, marking his first outdoor All-American honor in his NCAA Outdoor Championship debut. Khchina also made his debut at this level, finishing 14th overall in the 1500 meters with a time of 3:39.23 to secure his first outdoor All-American recognition of his collegiate career.
The women’s team from South Carolina is scheduled to compete in nine events on Thursday, beginning with the 4×100 meter relay at 8:05 p.m. Eastern Time. Seven semifinal rounds are planned for tomorrow’s schedule. Jathiyah Muhammad will participate in the women’s pole vault final at 8:35 p.m., while Tristen Harris will compete in the women’s long jump final at 9:40 p.m.
The men’s individual results included Crumpton placing sixteenth in the semifinals for the 400 meters and Khchina placing fourteenth in the semifinals for the 1500 meters.
South Carolina concludes its men’s outdoor season with both athletes achieving Second Team All-American status, as attention turns to upcoming performances by members of its women’s team.
